# CG-REQ-036: Request default value changed

The default of a request parameter or property changed.

**Why it matters:** Defaults define behaviour for omitted values.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Requests](./#req) |
| Direction | request |
| Detects | `schema.defaultChanged` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> Default of {where} changed.
>
> Consumers that omit the value get different behaviour if the provider applies defaults.
>
> **Fix:** Keep the previous default, or announce the behaviour change.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: default 20 → 50

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 20}}]
+       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 50}}]
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, medium. Default of GET /x: query parameter "limit" changed.

### Fires: default added (includeEquivalentChanges)

With options: `{"includeEquivalentChanges":true}`

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer}}]
+       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 20}}]
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Informational, info. Default of GET /x: query parameter "limit" changed.

### Does not fire: default added

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer}}]
+       parameters: [{name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 20}}]
        responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- Whether the provider applies defaults is outside the specification.
